# Oya Factory — full description

> Oya Factory runs Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode side by side with a built-in team of agents, checks every turn with your project's own tests, and rewinds any turn. Free, open source, for macOS and Windows.

Website: https://oyafactory.com/
Download: https://github.com/OyadotAI/keel-releases/releases/latest
Source: https://github.com/OyadotAI/keel (MIT licence)
Made by: Oya (https://oya.dev)

## In one line

Agents write code fast.Know it works before you merge.

Oya Factory runs Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode side by side, runs your project's own checks after every turn, and lets you rewind any turn. Ship what your agents write without reading every line twice.

Used by engineers at Amazon, Google, Salesforce and other companies.

## Why engineers switch

### Every turn is checked, not trusted

Your make check, tests and lint run after each turn, and the verdict sits beside the reply. A turn that fails its checks is never committed for you. Other agent apps show you what the agent said; Oya Factory shows you whether it works.

### Undo any turn, instantly

A snapshot is taken before every turn. When an agent goes sideways, rewind to the moment before it — and if you change your mind, the rewind itself can be undone. No git reflog archaeology.

### Five agents, zero collisions

Every task gets its own branch and worktree, and Oya Factory refuses to let two agents write the same working tree. Run Claude and Codex in parallel without one sweeping up the other's half-written files.

### Projects set up right, automatically

Oya Factory scans your repository, adds an agent team and the skills your stack needs, and keeps them current as it improves. Your agents start every task with the right instructions.

### Light, private and free

A native app on your system's webview, not a bundled browser. No account, no server of ours between you and your code, no step limits. MIT licensed, on macOS and Windows.

## The platform

### A team of agents, built in

Every project gets a product manager, a designer, a principal engineer, QA, a reviewer, security and reliability — subagents your coding agent calls in order: scope, design, plan, build, review, test. Tag one with @pm or @qa from the chat. Oya Factory keeps the team current as it improves.

### Skills, managed for you

Oya Factory recommends the skills your stack needs, adds them, and keeps them current. Write your own in a form, or browse a catalog.

### Plugins, MCP servers and tools

Skills, subagents, MCP servers, plugins, hooks and commands for every agent, in one Extensions screen. Recommended plugins install themselves in trusted projects.

### Every project, one window

Open all your repositories side by side in one sidebar, each with its own engine, its own lanes and its own state.

### Many lanes per project

A lane is one task: its own conversation, its own agent, and on its own branch when you want it. Run several at once; Attention tells you which one needs you.

### Agentic mode

The conversation in the centre: agents work, you steer, review the turns and answer what they ask.

### Coding mode

An editor in the centre with files, source control and the terminal, the agent beside you. Edit, save with ⌘S, accept suggestions with Tab.

## Features

- **Your checks, every turn**: Your project's own make check, tests or lint run after each turn, and the verdict sits beside the reply.
- **Rewind any turn**: A snapshot before every turn. Undo what an agent did without touching what you did.
- **Stage one hunk**: Keep three of an agent's four edits. Hunks are matched by content, so nothing stages at the wrong place.
- **Issue to pull request**: Start a task from a GitHub issue on its own branch, send corrections, and publish one traceable PR.
- **Recurring tasks**: A saved instruction on a schedule — nightly dependency checks, weekly cleanups — each run on its own branch.
- **A browser for your agents**: Each lane gets its own browser tab, so an agent can test the page it just built without touching yours.
- **Point at the pixel**: Click an element in the live preview, say what should change, and see whether the right file changed.
- **Find in the terminal**: ⌘F through an agent's scrollback, and quick commands you save once and run from anywhere.
- **Set up right, automatically**: An agent team, recommended skills and a readiness scan, kept current as Oya Factory improves.

## Compared with running an agent in a terminal

| | Oya Factory | An agent in a terminal |
|---|---|---|
| Each task on its own branch and worktree | Yes, automatically | By hand |
| Your project's checks after every turn | Yes, verdict beside the reply | If you remember to run them |
| Rewind a turn | Yes, a snapshot before each | git reflog, carefully |
| Permission prompts | Questions in the conversation | A prompt in whichever pane |
| Several agents at once | Yes, never two in one working tree | Several terminals, one checkout |
| Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode | All four, one workspace | One CLI per window |

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Oya Factory?

Oya Factory is a free, open-source desktop app for running AI coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode — on your own repositories. Each task runs in its own git branch and worktree, and every diff, command, approval and check result is shown as it happens.

### Which coding agents does it support?

Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity and OpenCode. Oya Factory drives the agent CLIs you already have installed and signed in, so it uses your existing subscriptions.

### Is Oya Factory free?

Yes. It is MIT licensed, with no account, no license key and no limit on agent steps.

### Which platforms does it run on?

macOS and Windows.

### Does Oya Factory send my code anywhere?

Oya Factory runs on your machine and has no server of its own in between. Your agents talk to their own providers exactly as they do in a terminal.

### How is it different from running an agent in a terminal?

A terminal shows text. Oya Factory gives every task its own branch, runs your project's checks after each turn, checkpoints every turn so it can be rewound, turns permission prompts into questions in the conversation, and lets several agents work at once without sharing a working tree.

### Do I have to change my repository?

No. It works on any git repository. It can optionally add an agent team, recommended skills and a readiness scan, which it keeps current.

### How does it compare to Orca or Conductor?

See the side-by-side pages for Orca and Conductor. In short: Oya Factory focuses on proving each turn — checks, rewind, clean branches — on macOS and Windows; Orca adds remote hosts and a phone app; Conductor is a polished Mac-only app.

## Oya Factory vs Orca

Orca runs agents.Oya Factory proves their work.

Running several agents in parallel worktrees is table stakes. The hard part is trusting what they wrote. Oya Factory is built around that: every turn checked, every turn reversible, every agent kept out of the others' way.

### Your checks run on every turn

After each turn, Oya Factory runs your project's own checks and puts the verdict beside the reply. A turn that fails is never committed for you. Orca leaves verifying a turn to you.

### Any turn can be rewound

A snapshot is taken before every turn, so a bad one is undone in a click — and the undo can be undone. No digging through git history.

### Two agents never share a working tree

The daemon refuses a second writer on the same checkout, across lanes and windows, so parallel agents can't sweep up each other's half-written files.

### Projects configured for you

A readiness scan, an agent team and the skills your stack needs, added and kept current automatically.

### Lighter on your machine

Oya Factory uses the webview your operating system already has, with a small Rust daemon per project. Orca is built on Electron, which ships its own copy of Chromium.

| | Oya Factory | Orca |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | MIT | MIT |
| Price | Free | Free |
| App shell | Tauri, your OS's webview | Electron, bundled Chromium |
| Checks verdict on every turn | Built in | — |
| Rewind any turn | Built in | — |
| One writer per working tree | Enforced | — |
| Automatic project setup | Built in | — |

Orca details are from orca.dev and its documentation as of 23 November 2026; “—” means its documentation does not describe the feature.

Page: https://oyafactory.com/compare/orca/

## Oya Factory vs Conductor

Conductor is a Mac app.Oya Factory is yours, everywhere.

Conductor made parallel agents feel polished on a Mac. Oya Factory brings the same workflow to macOS and Windows, open source and free, and adds proof: your checks on every turn, and agents that never collide.

### macOS and Windows

One app, one workflow, on both platforms. Conductor is macOS only.

### Free and open source

MIT licensed, no account and no paid tier. Read the code, change it, ship it.

### Your checks run on every turn

After each turn, Oya Factory runs your project's own checks and records the verdict beside the reply. A turn that fails is never committed for you.

### Your code stays on your machine

Everything runs locally; there is no cloud workspace and no server of ours between you and your repository.

### Projects configured for you

A readiness scan, an agent team and the skills your stack needs, added and kept current automatically.

| | Oya Factory | Conductor |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms | macOS and Windows | macOS |
| Licence | Open source, MIT | — |
| Price | Free | Paid Pro plan |
| Runs entirely on your machine | Yes | Also offers cloud workspaces |
| Checks verdict on every turn | Built in | — |
| One writer per working tree | Enforced | — |

Conductor details are from conductor.build and its documentation as of 23 November 2026; “—” means its site does not state it.

Page: https://oyafactory.com/compare/conductor/
